h: Why the Torah Says “Lech Lecha” Instead of “Depart”

p: "וַיֹּאמֶר ה' אֶל אַבְרָם: לֶךְ לְךָ מֵאַרְצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ",
"And Hashem said to Avram: Go for yourself from your land, etc., to the land that I will show you,"
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "לֶךְ לְךָ מֵאַרְצְךָ",
one must understand why it says 'Go for yourself from your land,'
דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר "צֵא מֵאַרְצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר וְלֵךְ אֶל הָאָרֶץ וְגוֹמֵר".
since it should have said: 'Depart from your land, etc., and go to the land, etc.'
(וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ עח עַמּוּד ב) דִּקְדֵּק עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיֵּלֶךְ אַבְרָם כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֵלָיו ה'",
(And in the holy Zohar 78b) it analyzed what is stated: 'And Avram went as Hashem had spoken unto him,'
דְּלָא כְתִיב "וַיֵּצֵא אַבְרָם" אֶלָּא "וַיֵּלֶךְ", כְּדִבּוּרוֹ "לֶךְ לְךָ".
for it is not written 'and Avram departed,' but rather 'and he went,' corresponding to His expression 'Go for yourself.'
וְשָׁם מוּבָן, כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב "כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר וְגוֹמֵר" וְהַדִּבּוּר הָיָה "לֶךְ לְךָ",
And there it is understood, since it is written 'as He had spoken, etc.,' and the divine speech was 'Go for yourself,'
אֲבָל לָמָּה גַּם בַּדִּבּוּר לֹא כְתִיב "צֵא מֵאַרְצְךָ"?
yet why in the divine speech itself was it not written 'Depart from your land'?
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "דְּהָא יְצִיאָה עֲבַדוּ בְּקַדְמִיתָא וְכוּלֵי",
And as for what the holy Zohar wrote: 'for they had already made a departure previously, etc.,'
שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁבָּא לְתָרֵץ זֶה,
which seems to resolve this,
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ מְדַקְדֵּק דִּבְסוֹף הַפָּסוּק כְּתִיב: "בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵחָרָן",
the holy Zohar later points out that at the end of the verse it is written: 'at his departure from Charan';
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: "מֵחָרָן כְּתִיב, וְהַהִיא יְצִיאָה מֵאֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ הֲוַת בְּקַדְמִיתָא".
and upon this Rabbi Elazar noted: 'from Charan it is written, whereas that departure from his birthplace had occurred previously.'
וְאִם כֵּן כָּאן בַּצִּיוּוּי דִּכְתִיב "לֶךְ לְךָ מֵאַרְצְךָ וּמִמּוֹלַדְתְּךָ",
And if so, here in the commandment where it is written 'Go for yourself from your land and from your birthplace,'
וְקָאֵי עַל יְצִיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה,
which refers to the initial departure,
וְאִם כֵּן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר: "צֵא מֵאַרְצְךָ וְגוֹמֵר וְלֵךְ אֶל הָאָרֶץ".
if so, it ought to have stated: 'Depart from your land, etc., and go to the land!'

h: The Zohar: Rectifying Your Own Spiritual Rank

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "לֶךְ לְךָ – לְאַתְקָנָא גַּרְמָךְ, לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ וְכוּלֵי",
However, the matter is according to what is written in the holy Zohar: ''Go for yourself'—to rectify yourself, to rectify your own spiritual rung, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ, שֶׁאַף שֶׁנּוֹלַד מִתֶּרַח שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
meaning He conveyed to him that even though he was born of Terach who was an idolater,
וּבְמָקוֹם שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁטוּפִין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
and in a locality where they were completely immersed in idolatry,
לֹא יִפְחַד מִזֶּה, שֶׁאַדְּרַבָּה, מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ יוּכַל לֵילֵךְ וּלְהַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָתוֹ.
he should not fear this, for on the contrary, out of that very background he could advance and achieve his sublime level.
וְעַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם מִשָּׁם אֶת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּמָצָאתָ וְגוֹמֵר",
And in the manner of what is stated: 'And from there you shall seek Hashem your God, and you shall find Him, etc.,'
וְהוּא אַחַר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וֶהֱפִיץ ה' אֶתְכֶם בָּעַמִּים וְגוֹמֵר",
which appears after it is said: 'And Hashem shall scatter you among the peoples, etc.,'
אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם לְהִתְיָאֵשׁ פֶּן חַס וְשָׁלוֹם תִּתְקַלְקְלוּ לְגַמְרֵי,
let not your heart faint into despair lest you become utterly corrupted, Heaven forbid,
כִּי אַדְּרַבָּה, מִשָּׁם דַּיְיקָא "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר",
for on the contrary, specifically from that place 'you shall seek, etc.,'
שֶׁהַגָּלוּת יִגְרוֹם "כִּי תִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל נַפְשֶׁךָ", וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה "וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם וּמָצָאתָ".
as the exile itself will catalyze: 'when you search for Him with all your heart and with all your soul,' and through this: 'you shall seek and find.'
וְכֵן אָמַר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ: "לֶךְ לְךָ" – לְאַתְקָנָא דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ,
And so Hashem, blessed be He, said to Avraham our Father: ''Go for yourself'—to rectify your spiritual rung,'
מֵאַרְצְךָ וּמוֹלַדְתְּךָ שֶׁנּוֹלַדְתָּ בְּמָקוֹם גָּרוּעַ וְשָׁפֵל,
from your land and your birthplace, where you were born into a degraded and lowly environment,
וּמִבֵּית אָבִיךָ שֶׁהָיָה תֶּרַח עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה –
and from the house of your father, Terach having been an idolater—
מִזֶּה עַצְמוֹ תּוּכַל לְתַקֵּן דַּרְגָּא דִילָךְ.
from that very source you will be able to rectify your own spiritual stature.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 2:30:1: ““Go for yourself from your land,” and so forth. As written in the Midrash on Ecclesiastes and in Tanchuma, Vayakhel: A person has three names. The first is the one others call him: that is, the human disposition he learns from others. This is “from your land.” Corresponding to it is “I will make you a great nation”: an entire nation from whom to learn, so that learning from others can also be good and need not be left behind. The second is the name his father calls him, as they said, “A father confers upon his son,” and, “A ewe follows a ewe.” This is “from your father’s house.” Corresponding to it is “I will make your name great,” from Abram to Abraham, after “I have made you the father of a multitude of nations”: he is a father to the entire world, and the paternal house is also good. The third is the name recorded in the account of his birth: his inborn nature, as written in Shabbat, “One who is born under Mars,” and so forth. This is “from your birthplace.” Corresponding to it is “I will bless you”—in your inborn nature. One must go beyond these; yet the movement is not to the opposite extreme, but “to the land that I will show you,” to the place where the spirit of the blessed God directs. At times God’s will lies in that very trait which appears inferior, as is known.”

sourceExcerpt.en: “Go for yourself from your land,” and so forth. As written in the Midrash on Ecclesiastes and in Tanchuma, Vayakhel: A person has three names. The first is the one others call him: that is, the human disposition he learns from others. This is “from your land.” Corresponding to it is “I will make you a great nation”: an entire nation from whom to learn, so that learning from others can also be good and need not be left behind. The second is the name his father calls him, as they said, “A father confers upon his son,” and, “A ewe follows a ewe.” This is “from your father’s house.” Corresponding to it is “I will make your name great,” from Abram to Abraham, after “I have made you the father of a multitude of nations”: he is a father to the entire world, and the paternal house is also good. The third is the name recorded in the account of his birth: his inborn nature, as written in Shabbat, “One who is born under Mars,” and so forth. This is “from your birthplace.” Corresponding to it is “I will bless you”—in your inborn nature. One must go beyond these; yet the movement is not to the opposite extreme, but “to the land that I will show you,” to the place where the spirit of the blessed God directs. At times God’s will lies in that very trait which appears inferior, as is known.

Abraham’s birth from Terah follows only the Sages’ statement, “Through everything the Holy One carries out His mission”; he is not on that account to be attributed to Terah.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Takanat HaShavin 4:2: “Although the perfection of this fourth level lies in the future, when complete redemption comes through the Messiah descended from David, who will clarify and reveal all the levels of repentance in their proper perfection, the light of this level already began to be revealed through Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, a descendant of King David. This is Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, as stated in Sanhedrin. He is called “Zerubbabel” because he was sown in Babylon: he was the principal redeemer from Babylon. This resembles what they said on “There the calf shall graze,” concerning the Messiah growing up with them in their country, just as Moses our teacher grew up in the palace of Egypt. The redeemer is always specifically one of the leading figures of the country of exile, in the manner of “From the forest itself comes the axe [that cuts it].” Zerubbabel was sown there: his very conception came about through the king of Babylon himself, as they said in Vayikra Rabbah, “They persuaded the governess, the governess persuaded the queen, and the queen persuaded the king.” For Jeconiah had already been sentenced, “Record this man as childless,” and so forth, but being in Babylon brought about [his having offspring], for the exile atoned, as they said in Sanhedrin. His conception showed that the Babylonian exile had already accomplished its work, and consequently redemption begins through him. His name therefore expresses his distinction: redemption grows through him. It would have been fitting for redemption then to be complete, but sin prevented it, as they said in Berakhot.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 16:1: “A Jew must not despair of anything: whether in bodily matters—as they said, “Even if a sharp sword rests upon a person’s neck, he must not refrain from seeking mercy”—or in matters of the soul. Even if he has sunk wherever he has sunk, and has sinned in a matter of which the Sages said that repentance does not avail, God forbid, or that repentance is difficult; or if he sees himself sinking ever further into the affairs of this world, he must not despair of himself and say that he can no longer break away. There is no despair at all for a Jew, and the blessed God can help in every matter. The entire building of the Israelite nation occurred after complete despair: “Abraham and Sarah were old,” and “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children?” No one any longer imagined believing this, even after the angel’s promise.”

h: The Hidden Purpose of the Promised Land

p: וְאָמַר לוֹ: "אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ",
And He said to him: 'To the land that I will show you,'
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י מִבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "וְלָמָּה לֹא גִּלָּה לוֹ? כְּדֵי לְחַבְּבָהּ בְּעֵינָיו וְכוּלֵי",
and Rashi explained from Bereishit Rabbah: 'And why did He not reveal it to him? In order to endear it in his eyes, etc.,'
וְהֵבִיא מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּעֲקֵידָה "קַח נָא וְגוֹמֵר".
and cited from what is stated concerning the Binding of Isaac: 'Take now, etc.'
אַךְ עֲדַיִן לֹא יִתְיַשֵּׁב, דְּשָׁם עַל כָּל פָּנִים גִּלָּה לוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ,
Yet this is still not settled, for there He revealed it to him afterward at any rate,
אֲבָל כָּאן לֹא נִזְכַּר כְּלָל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ הָאָרֶץ!
whereas here it is not mentioned at all that the identity of the land was ever verbally communicated to him!
אַךְ הָרַמְבַּ"ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה כָּתַב:
However, the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote:
"'וַיֵּרָא ה' אֶל אַבְרָם וַיֹּאמֶר לְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתֵּן אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת' – אָז נִתְקַיֵּם 'אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ'", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
''And Hashem appeared unto Avram and said: Unto your seed will I give this land'—only then was fulfilled: 'To the land that I will show you,'' see there,
וְיִהְיֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶךָּ" כְּמוֹ "אֲשֶׁר אַרְאֶה לְךָ",
and the meaning of 'that I will show you (ar'ekka)' is 'wherein I will appear unto you,'
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה' הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו",
and this is why Scripture states: 'And he built there an altar unto Hashem Who appeared unto him,'
שֶׁהוֹדָה עַל שֶׁנִּרְאָה אֵלָיו,
giving thanks for His having appeared unto him,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה' וְגוֹמֵר".
and subsequently it is written: 'And he built there an altar unto Hashem, etc.'

h: The Two Altars: Revealed and Concealed Spiritual Levels

p: אַךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ אִיתָא (פ עַמּוּד א):
Yet in the holy Zohar it is stated (80a):
"וּבָנָה תְּרֵין מַדְבְּחָן, חַד לְדַרְגָּא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא וְחַד לְדַרְגָּא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא וְכוּלֵי,
'And he built two altars, one for the revealed rung and one for the concealed rung, etc.,
וּכְדֵין אִתְעַטַּר אַבְרָהָם מִדַּרְגָּא לְדַרְגָּא עַד דִּסְלִיק לְדַרְגֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵי",
and then Avraham was crowned from rung to rung until he ascended to his designated level, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁתֵּי מַדְרֵגוֹת:
meaning that there are two spiritual tiers:
"דַּרְגָּא דְּאִתְגַּלְיָא" הוּא מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם בּוֹ תְּפִיסָה וְהַבָנָה,
the 'revealed rung' is that in which a person possesses cognitive grasp and understanding,
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה;
and this is attained through words of Torah;
וְ"דַרְגָּא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא" – מַה שֶּׁנֶּעְלָם הַהַנְהָגָה מִן הָאָדָם,
whereas the 'concealed rung' is where divine guidance is hidden from man's perception,
עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי ה' יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
in the manner of that which is stated: 'For Hashem shall be your confidence (bekhislekha), etc.,'
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י מִיְרוּשַׁלְמִי: "בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁאַתָּה כְּסִיל בָּהֶם".
and Rashi explained from the Yerushalmi: 'in matters regarding which you are foolish (clueless).'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל יִשְׁמָעֵאל: "לוּ יִשְׁמָעֵאל יִחְיֶה לְפָנֶיךָ",
And this is like Avraham our Father, peace be upon him, who prayed over Yishmael: 'O that Yishmael might live before You,'
וְכֵן יִצְחָק שֶׁרָצָה לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עֵשָׂו,
and similarly Yitzchak who intended to bless Eisav,
וְהוֹרָה לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתָּם,
and Hashem, blessed be He, guided them contrary to their conscious intent,
וְעַל זֶה אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה רַק תְּפִלָּה לַה',
and concerning this there is no remedy whatsoever other than prayer to Hashem,
וְאָז "וְשָׁמַר רַגְלְךָ מִלָּכֶד".
and then 'He shall keep your foot from being snared.'
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה'" וְלֹא כְּתִיב "הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו",
And this is what is stated afterward: 'And he built there an altar unto Hashem,' and it is not written 'Who appeared unto him,'
וְהַיְינוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּאִתְכַּסְיָא;
which corresponds to the concealed rung;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'", וְתַרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס: "וְצַלִּי בִּשְׁמָא דַּה'", שֶׁעַל זֶה נִצְרָךְ תְּפִלָּה.
and this is why Scripture states: 'and called upon the name of Hashem,' translated by Onkelos: 'and he prayed in the Name of Hashem,' for over this prayer is essential.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב: "הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ הַנֶּגְבָּה",
And afterward it is written: 'journeying toward the South (ha-negbah),'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּדְרֵגַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיְתָה הָאַהֲבָה וּמִדָּתוֹ מִדַּת חֶסֶד,
meaning that the spiritual rung of Avraham our Father was love, and his divine attribute was Lovingkindness (Chesed),
וְכָל עִסְקוֹ הָיָה לְבָרֵר שֶׁתִּהְיֶה אַהֲבָתוֹ זַכָּה רַק לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַדּוֹ,
and his entire endeavor was to clarify that his love be purely devoted to Hashem, blessed be He, alone,
וְלֹא יָבוֹא בְּלִבּוֹ שׁוּם חֶמְדָּה מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
and that no lust for the affairs of this material world enter his heart;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ הַנֶּגְבָּה",
and this is what is written: 'journeying toward the South,'
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁדָּרְשׁוּ (תְּמוּרָה טז עַמּוּד א):
in the manner of what they expounded (Temurah 16a):
"'כִּי אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי' – בַּיִת שֶׁמְּנוּגָּב מִכָּל טוֹבָה",
''For you have given me a dry Southland'—a house drained and dried (menugav) of all worldly goodness,'
וְזֶהוּ דַּרְגָּא דְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה מְבָרֵר מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה חֶסֶד,
and this was the rung of Avraham who refined his attribute of Chesed,
שֶׁתִּהְיֶה זַכָּה לַה' וְלֹא יִתְעָרֵב שׁוּם חֶמְדָּה מֵעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
that it be pristine unto Hashem without any intermingling of worldly lust.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיִצְחָק שֶׁהָיְתָה מִדָּתוֹ פַּחַד יִצְחָק וְצִמְצוּם,
And this explains what is stated concerning Yitzchak whose attribute was the Fear of Yitzchak and contraction (Tzimtzum),
וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: "וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּאֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב",
and it is written of him: 'and he was dwelling in the Southland,'
שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ נִיחָא בְּמִדָּה זוֹ,
for he had complete serenity in this attribute,
שֶׁהָיָה מְבוֹרָר בְּמִדַּת הַצִּמְצוּם, הַפַּחַד וְהַיִּרְאָה.
having been perfected in the trait of contraction, awe, and fear.

paragraphs.text: Temurah 16a:11: “The Gemara cites yet another verse involving Achsah: “And she said: Give me a blessing; for that you have set me in the land of the South [negev], and you have given me springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs” (Joshua 15:19). She said to her father: You have given me a home dried [menugav] of all goodness. “And you have given me springs of water”; this is referring to a man who has nothing other than Torah, which is metaphorically called water. But as he is unable to provide me with food, how can I live? “And gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.” Caleb said to her: Does someone learned in Torah, who dwells in the upper worlds and the lower worlds, require that sustenance be requested for him? He certainly does not need it, as God will provide for him in merit of his Torah studies.”

h: The Midrashic interpretation and prayer and divine response

p: וּבִמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה הוּבָא בְּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל בָּעַי עַל זַרְעוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִפְּלוּ בָּעַי,
And in Midrash Rabbah, cited in Rashi's commentary, it notes that he prayed at Ai for his descendants that they should not fall at Ai,
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה נִזְכַּר כָּאן תְּפִלָּתוֹ,
and one must understand why his prayer is recalled here,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִילָה לְגַמְרֵי, שֶׁהֲרֵי נָפְלוּ שָׁם שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה אִישׁ?
since it did not prove completely effective, as thirty-six men fell there?
גַּם אִם הָיָה הַמְּכֻוָּון "וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'" עַל תְּפִלָּה זוֹ,
Furthermore, even if 'and called upon the name of Hashem' pointed to this specific prayer,
לֹא יוּבַן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּשׁוּבוֹ מִמִּצְרַיִם: "אֶל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקְרָא שָׁם אַבְרָם בְּשֵׁם ה'",
one cannot understand what is stated upon his return from Egypt: 'unto the place of the altar, etc., and Avram called there upon the name of Hashem,'
וְלָמָּה צִיֵּיר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בְּסִימָן זֶה שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל שָׁם?
for why identify the altar specifically by the sign that he had prayed there?
אַךְ עִנְיַן הַמִּזְבְּחוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
Rather, the mystery of the altars is as we stated:
שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם כְּתִיב "וַיֵּרָא ה' אֶל אַבְרָם",
for earlier it is written: 'And Hashem appeared unto Avram,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵאִיר לוֹ שָׁם,
meaning that He illuminated unto him there,
וּכְתִיב: "לְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתֵּן אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת";
and it is written: 'Unto your seed will I give this land';
מִלַּת "הַזֹּאת" מוֹרָה שֶׁהֵאִיר לוֹ מִדַּת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁמּוֹרָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
the word 'this' (ha-zot) demonstrates that He illuminated unto him the attribute of the Land, which points to the Oral Torah,
וְהֵאִיר לוֹ כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁהָיָה מְפוֹרָשׁ לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו, שֶׁיִּתָּכֵן לוֹמַר לְשׁוֹן "הַזֹּאת",
and He shone it to such an extent that it was tangible before his eyes, such that the phrasing 'this' was appropriate,
שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה תָּמִיד לְשׁוֹן "זֶה" אוֹ "זֹאת",
for the term 'this' (zeh or zot) always indicates
שֶׁהוּא מְבוֹרָר בַּלֵּב עַד שֶׁהוּא כְּעוֹמֵד לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו,
that a matter is so clear in the heart that it stands as if visible before one's eyes,
כְּמוֹ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "זֶה אֵלִי",
as at the parting of the Red Sea where they proclaimed: 'This is my God,'
וּכְמוֹ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף תַּעֲנִית).
and as in the future when everyone will point with his finger (as written at the end of Ta'anit).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה' הַנִּרְאֶה אֵלָיו",
And this is what is stated: 'And he built there an altar unto Hashem Who appeared unto him,'
וְהוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּשְׁאַר שָׁם מָקוֹם קָבוּעַ וְקָדוֹשׁ לְהַשִּׂיג שָׁם תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and this was so that there remain a permanent, holy site to attain the Oral Torah,
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עִיקַּר תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
which was the core of the Torah study of Avraham our Father,
שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַכֹּל מִלִּבּוֹ,
who perceived everything out of his heart,
שֶׁכִּלְיוֹתָיו נַעֲשׂוּ כִּשְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא).
his kidneys becoming like two teachers instructing him in Torah and wisdom, as written (in Bereishit Rabbah 61).
וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה נִשְׁאָר הַקְּדוּשָׁה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, שֶׁהָרְשִׁימוּ נִשְׁאָר,
And wherever there is a dwelling of the Divine Presence, holiness endures forever, as the spiritual imprint remains;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (יוֹמָא לט עַמּוּד ב):
and as we find (Yoma 39b):
"פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַכְתִּי לְשִׁילֹה וְהֵרַחְתִּי רֵיחַ קְטוֹרֶת מִבֵּין כְּתָלֶיהָ",
'Once I walked to Shiloh and smelled the scent of incense between its walls,'
שֶׁאַף שֶׁכְּבָר חָרְבָה שִׁילֹה יָמִים רַבִּים נִשְׁאַר הָרְשִׁימוּ דִּקְדוּשָׁה וְהֵרִיחוּ רֵיחַ קְטוֹרֶת.
for even though Shiloh had been destroyed for many years, the impression of holiness lingered and they smelled the scent of incense.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מִזְבֵּחַ רִאשׁוֹן – מְקוֹם תּוֹרָה.
And this is the nature of the first altar—a conduit for Torah.

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִזְבֵּחַ הַשֵּׁנִי קָבַע לִמְקוֹם תְּפִלָּה,
And afterward the second altar he established as a sanctuary of prayer,
שֶׁרָצָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ הַנֶּגְבָּה",
wishing to pray regarding that which is stated: 'journeying toward the South,'
שֶׁרָצָה לְהִשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּמַדְרֵגָתוֹ וּמִדַּת חֶסֶד שֶׁלּוֹ,
desiring to achieve perfection in his spiritual level and his attribute of Chesed,
וְנִתְיָירֵא פֶּן יִכָּנֵס הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְיַכְנִיס בְּלִבּוֹ חֲמָדוֹת זָרוֹת וְאַהֲבַת עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
fearing lest the evil inclination intrude and plant foreign passions and worldly loves in his heart,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'", שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל זֶה וְקָבַע מְקוֹם תְּפִלָּה.
and concerning this Scripture states: 'and he called upon the name of Hashem,' for he prayed over this and established a station of prayer.
אַךְ לָמָּה בָּנָה מִזְבֵּחַ חָדָשׁ, וְהָיָה לוֹ לֵילֵךְ לְמִזְבֵּחַ רִאשׁוֹן וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל שָׁם עַל זֶה?
Yet why build a new altar when he could have returned to the first altar to pray there over this?
עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה בָּעַי הִתְפַּלֵּל שָׁם עַל בָּנָיו,
To this they stated in Midrash Rabbah that because he stood at Ai, he prayed there for his children,
שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁעֲתִידִין לְהִכָּשֵׁל שָׁם, וְהִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא יִתְקַלְקְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
foreseeing that they were destined to stumble there, and beseeching that they not be corrupted, Heaven forbid;
וְהַמְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל חֲבֵירוֹ וְהוּא צָרִיךְ לְאוֹתוֹ דָבָר – הוּא נַעֲנֶה תְּחִלָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא קַמָּא צב עַמּוּד א),
and he who pleads for mercy for his fellow when he himself needs that very thing is answered first (Bava Kamma 92a),
וְהוֹעִילָה תְּפִלָּתוֹ לְעַצְמוֹ.
and his prayer proved effective for himself.

Rava said to Rabba bar Mari: From where is this matter derived whereby the Sages stated: Anyone who asks for compassion from Heaven on behalf of another, and he requires compassion from Heaven concerning that same matter, he is answered first? Rabba bar Mari said to him that the source for this is as it is written: “And the Lord changed the fortune of Job, when he prayed for his friends” (Job 42:10).’

h: The exile and redemption and Avraham’s devotion

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְמִצְרַיִם, עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ, וְיָצָא מִשָּׁם עִם הַמַּתָּנוֹת,
And afterward when he entered Egypt, the nakedness of the earth, and emerged from there with the gifts,
כְּתִיב: "וַיַּעַל אַבְרָם מִמִּצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר הַנֶּגְבָּה",
it is written: 'And Avram went up from Egypt, etc., toward the South,'
וּכְתִיב: "וְאַבְרָם כָּבֵד מְאֹד בַּמִּקְנֶה וְגוֹמֵר",
and it is written: 'And Avram was very heavy in cattle, etc.,'
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זְצוּקַלְלָהּ"ה שֶׁהָיָה כָּבֵד עָלָיו וּלְמַשָּׂא כְּבֵדָה הַקִּנְיָנִים שֶׁקָּנָה,
and our holy master (Rabbi Mordechai Yosef of Ishbitz), of blessed memory, explained that the acquisitions he acquired felt heavy upon him as an oppressive burden,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּתְיָירֵא פֶּן יִכָּנֵס בְּלִבּוֹ חֶמְדַּת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
because he dreaded lest the desires of this world enter his heart,
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, דְּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי כְּתִיב "הַנֶּגְבָּה" שָׁם.
and it is as we explained, which is why 'toward the South' is written there.
וּכְתִיב: "וַיֵּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר אֶל מְקוֹם הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקְרָא שָׁם אַבְרָם בְּשֵׁם ה'",
And it is written: 'And he went, etc., unto the place of the altar, etc., and Avram called there upon the name of Hashem,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָלַךְ לְשָׁם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עוֹד שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְהַסְטִינוֹ.
meaning he returned there to pray further that the evil inclination not enter to seduce him.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 10:8: “Abraham our father also went into exile in Egypt, and this was one of his trials. The trials clarified that his firmness served the blessed God’s will. The proof was that, in response to God’s will, he was not obstinate: he set aside his own opinion and went into exile in Egypt. This is the power of a heart of flesh, the opposite of obstinacy. Therefore he received gifts there, whereas he did not wish to benefit from Sodom’s property. There [in Egypt] the matter came from the attribute of a heart of flesh, without obstinacy, so it was also permitted to enjoy its benefit. The episode of the kings, however, appeared outwardly to involve great obstinacy: one man fought four kings for his nephew Lot, something he had not done in Egypt for his wife, whom he loved more. Therefore in this case he did not wish to benefit, for in a matter that involves obstinacy one must clarify whether it is obstinacy for one’s own enjoyment or only for the honor of Heaven.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 5: ““He built an altar there to the Lord, and called upon the name of the Lord.” Abraham our father’s first trial was “Go for yourself”: poverty and restriction. In this a person must first be tested and refined, so as not to complain against the blessed God, God forbid. Rather, he should ask God that he not fall into the grinding pressures of poverty that cause a person to transgress his Creator’s will. The essential pressure of poverty is when a person is not content with his portion and desires unnecessary extras; he must ask God not to desire them. Thus it is written of Jacob, “Jacob was a whole man”: he was whole within himself, without craving unnecessary things, accepting with love what accords with the Creator’s will. Such were Abraham our father’s prayers in the first trial: to be content with his portion and not suffer poverty’s grinding pressure. This is “he called upon the name of the Lord”: that poverty should not, God forbid, cause him to transgress his Creator’s will. Therefore, when he returned from Egypt it says, “Abram was very heavy.” After he had been completely refined through poverty in the first trial, “very heavy” expresses a burden: he feared for himself because of his wealth, like King Solomon’s prayer, “Give me neither poverty nor riches.””

sourceExcerpt.he: "וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ לַה' וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'". נִסָּיוֹן הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה "לֶךְ לְךָ", הַיְינוּ עֲנִיּוּת וְצִמְצוּם, כִּי בָּזֶה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהִתְבָּרֵר תְּחִלָּה שֶׁלֹּא יִתְרַעֵם עַל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, אַךְ שֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְדִקְדּוּקֵי עֲנִיּוּת שֶׁמַּעֲבִירִין אֶת הָאָדָם עַל דַּעַת קוֹנוֹ. וְעִיקַּר דִּקְדּוּקֵי עֲנִיּוּת הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְרוֹצֶה בַּמּוֹתָרוֹת, וְעַל זֶה צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִתְאַוֶּוה לַמּוֹתָרוֹת. כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיַעֲקֹב (בְּרֵאשִׁית כה, כז): "וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה שָׁלֵם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ מִבְּלִי שׁוּם תַּאֲוָה לַמּוֹתָרוֹת, רַק כְּפִי רְצוֹן הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ כֵּן יְקַבֵּל בְּאַהֲבָה. וְכֵן הָיוּ תְּפִלּוֹת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּנִּסָּיוֹן הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שָׂמֵחַ בְּחֶלְקוֹ וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ דִּקְדּוּקֵי עֲנִיּוּת; וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "וַיִּקְרָא בְּשֵׁם ה'", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָעֲנִיּוּת לֹא יַעֲבִירֶנּוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם עַל דַּעַת קוֹנוֹ. וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁחָזַר מִמִּצְרַיִם נֶאֱמַר: "וְאַבְרָם כָּבֵד מְאֹד", הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בַּעֲנִיּוּת בְּבֵירוּר גָּמוּר בַּנִּסָּיוֹן הָרִאשׁוֹן, נֶאֱמַר "כָּבֵד מְאֹד" לְשׁוֹן כְּבֵידוּת, שֶׁהָיָה יָרֵא לְנַפְשׁוֹ מִפְּנֵי הָעֲשִׁירוּת, כִּתְפִלַּת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח): "רֵאשׁ וָעֹשֶׁר אַל תִּתֶּן לִי".
sourceExcerpt.en: “He built an altar there to the Lord, and called upon the name of the Lord.” Abraham our father’s first trial was “Go for yourself”: poverty and restriction. In this a person must first be tested and refined, so as not to complain against the blessed God, God forbid. Rather, he should ask God that he not fall into the grinding pressures of poverty that cause a person to transgress his Creator’s will. The essential pressure of poverty is when a person is not content with his portion and desires unnecessary extras; he must ask God not to desire them. Thus it is written of Jacob, “Jacob was a whole man”: he was whole within himself, without craving unnecessary things, accepting with love what accords with the Creator’s will. Such were Abraham our father’s prayers in the first trial: to be content with his portion and not suffer poverty’s grinding pressure. This is “he called upon the name of the Lord”: that poverty should not, God forbid, cause him to transgress his Creator’s will. Therefore, when he returned from Egypt it says, “Abram was very heavy.” After he had been completely refined through poverty in the first trial, “very heavy” expresses a burden: he feared for himself because of his wealth, like King Solomon’s prayer, “Give me neither poverty nor riches.”

h: The voice is the voice of Yaakov

p: וּשְׁנֵי הַמִּזְבְּחוֹת הֵם כְּנֶגֶד קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת,
And the two altars correspond to the voice of Yaakov in synagogues and study halls,
דִּכְתִיב: "הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב":
for it is written: 'The voice is the voice of Yaakov':
"קָל" חָסֵר וָא"ו שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל תְּפִלָּה, "קוֹל" מָלֵא וָא"ו – קוֹל תּוֹרָה,
the deficient 'kol' points to prayer, while the full 'kol' with a Vav is the voice of Torah,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן כָּל קִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהוּא לוֹט.
and through this he was able to rectify all corruption of the serpent, embodied in Lot.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: "'וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת' – זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ,
And as written in Bereishit Rabbah: ''And the spirit of God hovered'—this is the spirit of Mashiach;
'עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם' – בִּזְכוּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לְמַיִם",
'over the face of the waters'—by merit of repentance, which is compared to water,'
וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם בָּא לִידֵי תְשׁוּבָה.
namely the trait of Fear from which one arrives at repentance.
וְכֵן תְּפִלָּה גַּם כֵּן מִמִּדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁהִיא יִרְאָה,
So too prayer stems from the attribute of Malchut, which is Fear,
וְנִדְרָשׁ תָּמִיד לְשׁוֹן יִרְאָה עַל תְּפִלָּה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר נֹחַ סוֹף מַאֲמָר ד).
and the term 'fear' is regularly expounded as prayer (as explained in Noach, end of discourse 4).
וּבְתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר אִיתָא (תִּקּוּן לו): "'עַל פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם' – וְלֵית מַיִם אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא",
And in Tikkunei Zohar it is brought (Tikkun 36): ''Over the face of the waters'—and there is no water other than Torah,'
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה יְכוֹלִים לְתַקֵּן כָּל קִלְקוּל הַנָּחָשׁ.
meaning that through Torah and prayer one can rectify all corruption of the serpent.
וְכָל הַפָּרָשָׁה הִיא רְמָזִים לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
And this entire Torah portion contains allegorical lessons for every soul of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּרְמַז בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה עַל כָּל נֶפֶשׁ, וְהוּא לִמּוּד לְכָל אֶחָד.
as the holy Zohar allegorized the entire portion upon each soul, serving as an instruction for everyone.
וְשַׁבָּת זְמַן מוּכָן לִתְשׁוּבָה
And Shabbat is a time prepared for repentance,
וְכֵן לִזְכּוֹת לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְעָמִים,
as well as to merit the Written Torah and Oral Torah, as has been explained several times,
וְיִזְכּוּ לִהְיוֹת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין.
and may they merit to be redeemed immediately.

sourceExcerpt.he: כַּיָּדוּעַ דְּאֵין כֹּחָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא בְּפִיהֶם (בַּמִּדְבָּר פָּרָשָׁה כ׳, וּמִדְרַשׁ תְּהִלִּים כ״ב, וּמְכִילְתָּא בְּשַׁלַּח פָּרָשָׁה ב׳, וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וַיִּשְׁלַח קע״ח עַמּוּד א׳, וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת), שֶׁהוּא "הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב" [בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ז:כ״ב], שְׁנֵי קוֹלוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (דִּפְתִיחְתָּא דְּאֵיכָה רַבָּתִי): בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת וּבְבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, הַיְינוּ קוֹל תְּפִלָּה הָרָמוּז בְּמִלַּת "הַקֹּל" חֲסַר וָא״ו בִּלְשׁוֹן הַכָּתוּב, וּבְתוֹסֶפֶת הַהֵ״א הָרוֹמֶזֶת לִתְפִלָּה כַּנּוֹדָע, וְ"קוֹל" מָלֵא וָא״ו רוֹמֵז לְקוֹל תּוֹרָה כַּיָּדוּעַ, דְּהַוָּא״ו רוֹמֶזֶת עַל זֶה (עַיֵּן בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וַיִּגַּשׁ ר״י רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳, וְרֵישׁ וַיִּקְרָא), וְהַשּׁוֹפָר הוּא רוֹמֵז הִתְעוֹרְרוּת קוֹל שׁוֹפָר דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא הַקּוֹל תּוֹרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם לְטוֹבָה.
